newsitem.title: BRAZIL: New Brazil council will work to boost coffee crop.
newsitem.headline: New Brazil council will work to boost coffee crop.

text.p: A new Brazilian policy-making coffee council will work to increase Brazil's coffee crop to an average of 30 million to 35 million 60-kg bags in the next 10 years, the Industry and Commerce Minister said.

"Brazil will have to develop and implement over the next decade a coffee policy which allows average production levels of 30 million to 35 million bags per crop year," said Francisco Dornelles at a ceremony marking the creation of the new council.
Brazilian coffee production in 1996/97 is estimated at between 25 million to 27 million bags and preliminary indications are of a smaller 1997/98 crop.
The council aims to boost output by creating better credit lines for farmers and looking at ways to boost productivity to an average 15 to 20 bags per hectare, Dornelles said.
In addition the council will improve the collection of statistical data and will also "stimulate a more aggressive stance on the part of the exporting sector with importing countries," he added.
The new council is made up of six representatives each from the private and the public sector and will be presided over by Dornelles.
Previously Brazilian coffee policy had been decided by discussions between the government and an informal private sector umbrella group.

"This is a very good beginning. The private sector can now organize itself and talk with the government on equal terms," said Sergio Coimbra, president of the Brazilian Soluble Coffee Industry Association.
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso who was present at today's ceremony also welcomed the formalisation of the relationship between the public and private sectors.
"We must defend our interests and those interests will only be defended if we act together," he said.
